name: block-row
description: One text block in a list of blocks: the text and, on hover, its actions. Kind "source" is a block to pick (Add; shaded once already used); kind "editable" has a drag handle, Edit / Delete and an in-place edit mode.

props.name: type
props.description: "source" or "editable".

props.name: text
props.description: The block's text.

props.name: included
props.description: Kind "source": the block is already in the document (row shaded, Add hidden).

rationale: Rows have no hairlines and no vertical rules, unlike table-row: Figma draws these panes as flat block lists on white, each row its text with a trailing blank line, so min-height is spacing.9 + spacing.6 (60px) and padding spacing.cell (10px). Hover and focus-within fill bg.surface-pressed. Actions and the drag icon are at opacity 0 until hover or focus (or edit mode), like table-row's hover-only icons, so a long list reads as text first; keyboard focus keeps them reachable. An already-included source block is shaded (Figma base/warm-100 in light, bg.surface-pressed in dark) and its Add button is visibility:hidden, not removed, so the row keeps its width. Edit mode swaps the text for a textarea with an accent border and drops the text padding, so the box sits where the text was. Drag and drop is driven by the host page through data-dragging (dimmed) and data-drop="before"/"after" (an accent line on the top or bottom edge), the same attribute API table-row offers. Not sourced from Figma: the hover / focus reveal of the actions. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Rows are <li> inside a <ul class="ds-block-list">; give the list an aria-label. Actions are real buttons; the drag handle is a plain element with a labelled icon (drag and drop has no keyboard equivalent here, the host page must offer one if it matters).

name: divider
description: A single 1px rule for separating two stacked sections (horizontal, Penpot's own instance) or two items in a row, e.g. grouped buttons in a table-header-actions bar (vertical, not from Penpot).

props.name: orientation
props.description: "horizontal" (default, Penpot's instance) renders a full-width, 1px, text-subactive rule for separating stacked sections. "vertical" (not sourced from Penpot) renders a small object-dark-passive square dot (spacing-1 x spacing-1), centered on its cross axis, for separating items within a horizontal row -- e.g. grouping buttons in a table-header-actions bar.

rationale: Penpot's "Divider" is a single main instance with one child rectangle, horizontal only; renamed to lowercase to satisfy the schema's name pattern. Horizontal: a full-width rule whose height is --ds-border-width-thin (1px) -- the border-width scale, because a hairline is a stroke, and spacing's smallest step (2px) would double its weight. Its fill is text.subactive, the token this system reserves for de-emphasized but visible content (table-cell's Source cell uses it for the same reason): enough contrast to read as a rule against bg.surface without competing with the text around it. No radius, no shadow: it is a flat rule. Vertical (not sourced from Penpot, which models only the horizontal instance): separates items within a horizontal row, e.g. grouped buttons in table-header-actions. It is a small square dot (spacing-1 x spacing-1), a design decision that replaced an earlier short vertical line, in object-dark.passive, the table border color, so it belongs to the same bordered vocabulary as the table around it; it is centered on the cross axis. Square, not round, because every radius token in the Base style resolves to 0 or 1px and a circle would be the one rounded shape in the system. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.

name: dropdown-menu
description: A floating menu of selectable action items, shown/hidden by a trigger element it's paired with (e.g. components/input-dropdown). Not a standalone widget — wrap a trigger and this menu together in a .ds-dropdown container to get real open/close/select behavior (see index.html). If the trigger uses input-dropdown's size="large" (100% width), mirror data-size="large" onto the .ds-dropdown wrapper too, so it switches to a block-level container the trigger can actually fill — see style.css.

props.name: items
props.description: Each item is a real .ds-dropdown-menu__item <button> child, not a JS-templated list — this component doesn't render from data, the consumer supplies the DOM. data-value on each item is read by component.js and included in the ds-dropdown-select event detail. An item of the form {'divider': true} renders a real divider/template.html <hr> instead of a button, grouping the items around it -- see rationale. With multiple=true an item may also carry selected (ticked) and mixed (the half-ticked box).

props.name: multiple
props.description: Checkbox items (explicit request 2026-10-01): the menu gets data-multiple and aria-multiselectable, each item a checkbox glyph before its label. A click toggles the item's aria-selected and keeps the menu open; ds-dropdown-select carries { value, label, selected, values }. The trigger's text is left alone.

props.name: scroll
props.description: Bounds the menu height (min of 320px and 45vh, override with --_menu-max-height) and scrolls the items inside it. For long lists such as a project picker in a popup.

rationale: Styled to Figma's opened dropdown (node 45:6594 of the application file), superseding the earlier Penpot values. The panel is bg.surface with a 1px border in the open trigger's base/750 (--ds-color-input-border-hover) and no shadow: the border is the edge, matching the trigger it belongs to. It sits 10px below the trigger (Figma's column gap, spacing-3 + spacing-1) and is exactly as wide as the trigger (border-box). Items are 44px rows with 10px padding, text on one line, touching edge to edge so the menu reads as one continuous surface; hover and keyboard focus fill bg.surface-pressed; the item matching the current value (aria-selected, kept by component.js) is Medium weight, so the current choice is visible without a checkmark. 10px and 44px have no spacing token and are composed from the scale (8+2, 40+4). A divider item composes the real divider component (declared in `uses`), drawn in object-dark.passive, the table rule color. A wrapper with data-size="large" or "compact" is block-level, so a full-width or 200px trigger can fill it. Not sourced from the design: open/close, positioning, outside-click and Escape to close, and aria-expanded toggling -- a static design tool doesn't model a floating layer, and without them this would be a picture of a menu. Items are in plain top-to-bottom DOM order, not the reversed authoring order of the Penpot instance, so the DOM order matches what is seen. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Multiple (explicit request 2026-10-01, no design source): each item shows the D_SYSTEM checkbox glyph (icons/checkbox, checkbox-selected, checkbox-semi-select) in table-cell's own checkbox colors, so a ticked item reads like a ticked row; all three glyphs are in the item and CSS shows the one for its state, as a row checkbox does. A ticked item keeps regular weight -- the box already says it is chosen. The menu stays open between clicks because ticking several values is the point.
a11y_notes: Menu container has role="listbox"; items have role="option". The trigger (paired via [data-dropdown-trigger] inside a .ds-dropdown wrapper) gets aria-expanded toggled automatically by component.js -- it must already carry aria-haspopup="listbox" itself (input-dropdown does). Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. Clicking outside the .ds-dropdown wrapper closes it. Keyboard (2026-10-03): ArrowDown/ArrowUp on the closed trigger open the menu; in the open menu they move focus between enabled items (wrapping), Home/End jump to the first/last, Enter/Space pick the focused item (native button click), Tab closes the menu and lets focus move on. Opening from the keyboard focuses the selected item, else the first; closing while focus is inside the menu returns it to the trigger. Items stay ordinary Tab-reachable buttons rather than a roving tabindex, so nothing extra is needed for a menu a host builds at runtime. A divider item renders role="separator" (divider's own template), not role="option" -- it's not a selectable choice and carries no data-value, so component.js's select-click listener has nothing to attach to it in the first place. Multiple: the listbox has aria-multiselectable="true" and each option's aria-selected is its ticked state; the glyphs are aria-hidden.

name: empty-state
description: A standalone empty-state block: optional icon, message, optional action button. For non-table-row empty states (a paper-preview with nothing selected, a set table with no blocks yet) -- a table-row-shaped empty cell should keep using table-cell's own type="empty-state" instead.

props.name: message
props.description: The empty-state text. Reuses table-cell's own Penpot-sourced empty-state string/typography as the default.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon name (matches an icons/<name>.svg file), shown above the message.

props.name: action_label
props.description: Optional action button label (e.g. "Add project"). Composes a real text-button instance (secondary, dotted underline -- the action stays on the current view, it doesn't navigate). Omit for a message-only empty state.

props.name: size
props.description: "row": a 44px row for an empty table or block list (centered caption at half opacity, hairline under it).

rationale:
The design source has no standalone empty-state component. table-cell's type="empty-state" is sourced, but is shaped as one table-row cell (no icon or action slot), so it can't represent an empty preview, picker or pane. This component reuses table-cell's sourced message styling (bodyTextItalic, text.subactive) and adds only the layout a cell can't offer: a centered column with an optional icon above the message and an optional action (a real text-button, declared in `uses`) below it. The icon size (spacing-8, 32px) is a judgment call, not sourced: larger than inline spacing-7 glyphs because it heads a standalone block. The action is secondary / dotted because adding something from an empty state happens in place rather than navigating away.

Sizes, from the application's Figma screens:
- data-size="row": the empty row under a table head or block list. One table row high (spacing.row plus the hairline), the caption role (Inter Italic 16px) in text.active, the whole row including its hairline at 50% opacity; the hairline is base/150 in light and the pressed surface in dark.
- data-size="block": the empty area inside a picker. Fills its row, 40px above and below, caption role at half opacity, on the pressed surface (base/50 in light).
- data-size="text": one plain left-aligned line at half opacity on the surface color, inset spacing.cell, no height or hairline of its own.
- data-size="fill": the empty box of a preview pane. Absolutely positioned 20px inside its positioned parent, filled with base.175 (a palette token, the same in both themes), a hairline on its left edge, the message centered, the whole box at half opacity.
Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: The icon is aria-hidden: the message already carries the full meaning. The action is a real, focusable <button> from text-button's template, with no accessibility gap beyond what that component documents.

name: figure
description: An image with its caption built in: the picture at its own proportions, full width of its container, and under it one grey italic line (who, where, when). Without a caption it is just the image; without an image it is a gray 16:9 placeholder.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. Omit it and the figure renders the gray 16:9 placeholder (data-empty).

props.name: alt
props.description: Text alternative of the image. Empty marks the image decorative, which is right when the caption already says what it shows.

props.name: caption
props.description: The line under the image. Omit it and no caption element is rendered.

rationale: Not drawn in Figma: the Portfolio preview needs a picture with a who / where / when line under it, and no existing component has a caption (paper-preview only has skeleton bars, gallery-image is a 160px thumbnail). Built on the semantic pair <figure> / <figcaption>, so the caption belongs to the image for assistive technology and for anyone reading the markup, with no wrapper logic. Every value is an existing token: the caption role (--ds-font-caption-*, Inter italic) in text-subactive, 4px (spacing-2) below the image, the object-dark-passive gray behind the image as in gallery-image, 16:9 for the empty state as in paper-preview's image placeholder. The image is never cropped (width 100%, height auto): portrait and landscape photos on one document sheet each keep their shape, which a fixed ratio with object-fit would not. Long unbroken captions wrap (overflow-wrap: anywhere) so a long place name cannot widen the sheet. Light and dark both come from the tokens; rendering verified in both themes.
a11y_notes: <figure>/<figcaption> ties the caption to the image. alt defaults to empty (decorative), because in the Portfolio the caption is the description; a host with no caption should pass a real alt. The caption color is text-subactive (black at 40% in light), which is below 4.5:1 on white: acceptable for supplementary credit lines, not for the only statement of anything important.

name: gallery
description: A horizontally-scrolling row (filmstrip/slider) of gallery-image thumbnails that functions as a real multi-select photo picker: click one (or several) to select it, each selected thumbnail shows its own selection-order badge (1st click = "1", 2nd = "2", ...), click again to deselect.
rationale:
Layout from Penpot's "Gallery" instance: a flex row, aligned start, column gap spacing-4 (12px), Token-bound. Penpot defines no overflow behavior (a fixed-width demo row with few images), so the row is a scrolling filmstrip (nowrap, overflow-x:auto, children flex-shrink:0), with spacing-3 (8px) padding top and bottom because overflow-x:auto also clips vertically, which would cut a selected image's outline. The demo holds 10 mixed-format images so the scroll is actually visible.

Selection (component.js, not sourced -- a static design tool doesn't model clicks): click to select, and each selected image shows a badge with its selection order; clicking again deselects and renumbers the rest so the order stays contiguous. The ordered selection is persisted to localStorage (key ds-gallery-selection:<gallery id>) and dispatched as ds-gallery-select, so another process or page can read it. The badge is accent-1, matching the selected image's outline, with a text-inverced numeral.

Scrollbar: the native one is hidden and replaced by a custom, always-visible bar in .ds-gallery-wrapper (outside the scrolling element, so it doesn't scroll away): a spacing-2 (4px) track in bg-surface-pressed with an accent-1 thumb sized to the visible fraction. It is interactive -- drag the thumb or click the track to scroll -- and grows to spacing-4 (12px) on hover and drag so it's easier to grab. It is absolutely positioned inside padding the wrapper reserves for the grown state, so growing never shifts layout. The row itself can be dragged to scroll with mouse or pen (touch already scrolls natively); a 4px threshold tells a drag from a click, and a drag never also toggles the image it ends on. Pointer capture is taken only once a drag is confirmed, because a captured pointer's click is delivered to the capturing element, which would stop plain clicks from reaching the images.

Reset: any element with data-gallery-reset="<gallery id>" clears that gallery's selection through the same path a click uses, via a ds-gallery-reset event, so a host (e.g. popup's gallery body) needs no gallery-specific code. The trigger is a two-step confirm: the first click arms it (label "Yes, reset selection", text-button's error status), the second resets and restores the original label and status; a click anywhere else while armed disarms it, the same outside-click mechanism dropdown-menu uses.

.ds-gallery-picker is a separate, plain scrolling row for gallery-image type="picker" cards: 10px gaps, native thin scrollbar, no custom scrollbar or drag-to-scroll. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: No list or grid role is added (Penpot's source has no such structure). Each composed gallery-image is a real control: role="button", tabindex="0", aria-pressed reflecting selection, Enter/Space toggle like a click. Placeholder images have no accessible name beyond the role; a host with real photos should add an aria-label per image. The scrollbar thumb has role="scrollbar", aria-orientation="horizontal", aria-controls pointing at the row, aria-valuenow/min/max as a 0-100 percentage, and tabindex="0" with ArrowLeft/Right (80% of the visible width) and Home/End -- needed because a native scroll container only answers arrow keys when it has focus itself. Drag-to-scroll has no keyboard equivalent of its own; the thumb and each image's Tab order cover the same range. Known gap: the reset trigger's armed state is not announced proactively (no live region); the button's accessible name does update, so re-reading it reveals the state.

name: gallery-image
description: One item of a gallery. type="image" (default): a thumbnail standing in for a photo, with an optional badge marking selection order. type="picker": a selectable 160px square card with an optional real image. type="text-icon": a text skeleton placeholder -- a bold label above a stack of gray bars, the last one shorter, in short / middle / full lengths -- selectable as a radio group with its text-icon siblings.

props.name: type
props.description: Sets data-type. "image" (default, attribute omitted in markup) renders the photo-thumbnail look, sized by the format prop below. "text-icon" renders the skeleton/placeholder look instead (120px fixed height, flexible width -- see rationale; format is not applicable in that case, Penpot only samples Text-icon at Format=landscape). Kebab-cased from Penpot's own Type axis (Image/Text-icon).

props.name: format
props.description: Only applies when type="image". Sets data-format, controlling width at a fixed 160px height: landscape (260px, wider), portrait (130px, narrower), square (160px, equal). Kebab-cased from Penpot's own Format axis (landscape/Portrait/Square).

props.name: selected
props.description: Sets data-selected, which every type renders as the same outline frame (see rationale). For type="image" the host also renders the .ds-gallery-image__badge child with the selection's order number (this component doesn't generate it). For type="text-icon" this only sets the initial state -- component.js wires single-select radio semantics across each group of text-icon siblings, so at most one card per group ends up selected at runtime.

props.name: subtype
props.description: Only applies when type="text-icon": short / middle / full, matching Penpot's Subtype axis. It determines how many .ds-gallery-image__bar children the template renders (1 full-width + 1 short for short, 2+1 for middle, 4+1 for full) and the label text.

props.name: src
props.description: Only applies when type="picker": URL of the picture, rendered as an (object-fit: cover, loading=lazy) over the placeholder fill. Omit for the placeholder. A failed load is hidden by component.js so the fill shows.

props.name: alt
props.description: Only applies with src: the 's alt text. Empty by default because the picker

rationale: type="image": sizes from Penpot's "Image" instances, all three formats sampled -- height 160px, width 260 / 130 / 160px for landscape / portrait / square (pixel-matched). The fill is a flat object-dark-passive gray standing in for a photo, as Penpot's own instances do (a flat-color rectangle, no image asset); a host sets a real background-image. Penpot's #ADADAD matches several tokens; object-dark-passive was chosen as the neutral, non-state fill. The selection badge (Penpot State="Selected") is a small square flush in the bottom-right corner: a text-inverced numeral in typography.heading5 on accent-1, the same color as the selected frame. Penpot's "Number-label" is a filled square with a text character, so it is HTML text, not an icon. The number and which images are selected are host state (gallery supplies them). Selected frame (all types): a 1px accent-1 outline. Hover (all types): a 1px text-active outline, no fill -- one shared affordance for both types. Outlines, not borders, so the pixel-matched sizes don't grow; hover is declared before selected so a hovered selected item keeps its accent outline. type="text-icon" (Penpot Subtype short / middle / full, purpose confirmed from Penpot's variants and exports): a skeleton placeholder -- the subtype's name as a bold label above flat gray bars standing in for lines of text, ending in one shorter 80px bar (short = 1+1 bars, middle = 2+1, full = 4+1). Boards are 120px high with spacing-6 (20px) padding; bar height and gaps are documented in style.css, including Penpot's visible overflow for middle and full. Width is not Penpot's 566px: the cards sit side by side and share their container (flex 1 1 0, min-width 0). Selection works as a radio group (component.js): siblings sharing a parent form one group, one selected at a time, with roving tabindex and arrow keys like native radios. type="picker": a selectable 160px square
a11y_notes: type="image" on its own is a static thumbnail; composed in gallery, gallery's component.js makes it a real toggle (role="button", tabindex, aria-pressed). A host with real photos should add an accessible label per image. type="picker" is a native <button> with aria-pressed. type="text-icon": the shared parent gets role="radiogroup", each card role="radio" with aria-checked, and a roving tabindex, so the group is one Tab stop; arrow keys move focus and selection together, Enter/Space select -- native radio behavior. Note: text-icon's real purpose is a loading skeleton, and a selectable skeleton isn't a real UI pattern; the selection exists to demonstrate the shared selected frame. Used purely as a loading state, wire no selection and mark the surrounding container role="status" / aria-busy instead.

name: header-block
description: The full header of a table: a title/tabs region (table-header) and an action-button cluster (table-header-actions), with an optional search, forming one header bar whose border-bottom separates it from the table's rows below.

props.name: size
props.description: big or small. Maps to Penpot's Size variant axis; controls the header's own padding scale (spacing.6/spacing.5 vs spacing.0/spacing.3). Does not affect table-header or table-header-actions content.

props.name: search
props.description: When true, renders a center search zone (composing input) between table-header and table-header-actions. Not a Penpot-sourced axis -- see rationale.

props.name: search_placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the search input, only rendered when search=true.

props.name: layout
props.description: bulk: the bulk-actions row over a table -- table-header-actions flush left (the actions act on selected rows; give them status 'disabled' until something is selected), plus, with search=true, an always-open search docked right. No table-header.

props.name: more_actions
props.description: layout='bulk' only: a second table-header-actions group, same item shape as actions, right after the first and set apart by divider's vertical dot (explicit request 2026-10-01: page-wide actions, then the selected rows' bulk actions).

props.name: search_plain
props.description: layout='bulk' with search=true: the field keeps input's own unboxed rest state (no border at rest) instead of header-block's boxed-at-rest search; input's hover and focus states as ever.

rationale:
Only Size is modeled as a variant. Penpot's other axis, Type (Archived / Found / Analysed / Queue / Queue-Small), changes only which title table-header renders and how many actions table-header-actions renders -- those components' own variants -- so modeling it here would duplicate their variant surfaces in a shell with no visual opinion about them.

data-size="big" (Figma header row): a plain 60px bg.surface row with 20px side padding, no gap between actions, no frame and no top padding, and one hairline under it -- the same hairline every table row has, so the header reads as the table's first row. data-size="small" keeps the earlier shaded bar: bg.surface-pressed with the border-width-thin / object-dark-passive border of table-cell's grid, inner padding spacing.3 (8px, Token-bound in Penpot's Queue/Small instance). Nested table-header's own chip background and border are reset inside the row so the two don't form a doubled box. The row is justify-content: space-between, which docks the title left and the actions right regardless of either's width. The divider Penpot draws under the header is not composed: the row's own border-bottom does that job, and a text.subactive divider against it would render as a doubled, two-tone line.

Search (not sourced from Penpot): one search box per table, filtering its rows. It composes input's template unchanged (no icon; the icon set has no search glyph). With a search, the row switches from space-between to flex-start + gap, because space-between only works for exactly two children. By default a "Search" trigger reveals the input and blurring an empty input collapses it back, so an unused field doesn't take header space; a non-empty input stays open. data-open="always" renders the input with no trigger, and data-align="end" docks the zone to the right edge. layout="bulk" is the bulk-actions row: table-header-actions flush left, an optional always-open search right, no title. The search field keeps a visible border through header-block's own rule, although input's transparent fill is borderless at rest. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. more_actions (bulk layout, explicit request 2026-10-01): a second action group after the first, set apart by divider's vertical dot -- the same dot this system already uses between actions -- so page-wide actions (Add, Fetch) and actions on the selected rows read as two groups in one reading line. search_plain: the field is input's own, unboxed at rest, for a header whose search shouldn't stand out as a box.
a11y_notes: The search input is input's plain native field; labeling is the host page's responsibility, as input documents. The search trigger and the input both stay in the DOM and component.js only flips which is visible (data-open) -- a show/hide of the same kind as popup and dropdown-menu.

name: header-tab
description: One panel in a full-width row of N equal-width section tabs (e.g. a For Review / Analysed / Archived / Filtered strip) -- each tab is its own flex:1 box with a background and border that change with selection, tiling edge to edge across the row. Distinct from table-header's type="2-tabs" (a single content-hugging chip holding both labels); see rationale. The host composes N instances inside a shared role="tablist" wrapper and typically renders a header-block bar below the strip for the active tab's own search and bulk actions.

props.name: active
props.description: Whether this tab is the current section. Sets aria-selected and switches background/text color/underline per rationale.

props.name: label
props.description: The tab's title text (e.g. "For Review").

props.name: count
props.description: Optional secondary caption rendered beside the label (e.g. "4 total, 5 submitted"). Omitted entirely from the DOM when not passed, matching table-header's own optional info caption.

props.name: size
props.description: "compact": 56px tabs for a pane head (see rationale); default is the 60px full-width strip.

rationale:
Read from the application's Figma file: the repeated "header" instance used identically across its section screens (nodes 150:16076 active / 150:16077 inactive), with only the active assignment changing. Height is a fixed 60px, the same as the nav bar it sits flush beneath; padding is Figma's 10px vertical / 20px horizontal. The label and count sit in an inner .ds-header-tab__text wrapper with Figma's bottom alignment and 10px gap, while the outer tab centers that block vertically -- Figma's own two-level structure.

Colors read off Figma's two states: active = bg.surface + text.active label; inactive = bg.surface-pressed + text.subactive label, the same active/inactive vocabulary table-header's 2-tabs uses. The count uses text.subactive in both states (Figma's 50% caption). Figma's 0.5px bottom border is drawn with border-width-thin in object-dark-passive, the pairing table-cell and table-header use for their borders, rather than a 0.5px-only token. The inactive label carries Figma's permanent dotted underline: it stays in the view when clicked (CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions).

Why not an extension of table-header's 2-tabs: that variant is one content-hugging chip holding both labels, sitting beside table-header-actions; here each tab independently stretches flex:1 across the whole row, carries its own background and border, and the strip sits above a separate header bar. None of 2-tabs' CSS transfers. Figma's "actions-block" child holds one invisible, unpopulated placeholder button on every instance and is not modeled.

data-size="compact" is a pane-head tab (Figma node 150:16299): 56px tall, 20px side padding, a hairline on the left of every tab (the divider between panes), the label in the "title" role, the count in the caption role and hidden while the tab is open. .ds-header-tabs holds tabs as a flex row. Not sourced from Figma: click-to-switch in component.js, scoped to the nearest role="tablist" ancestor because each tab is composed independently by the host; a tab row that never switches would be a dead affordance. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: A real role="tab" <button>, per the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern. The host wraps the tabs in a role="tablist" container (this component doesn't own that wrapper) and pairs each tab with its role="tabpanel". aria-selected reflects the active prop and is kept in sync on click by component.js. The focus-visible outline (accent-1, 2px, matching table-header's tabs) has no Figma equivalent: static design tools don't model keyboard focus.

name: input
description: A single-line text field for entering short freeform text. Use for names, search terms, notes — anything that isn't a fixed set of choices (use input-dropdown for that).

props.name: type
props.description: "text" (default, a single-line <input>) or "textarea" (a multi-line <textarea>, not from Penpot -- see rationale).

props.name: fill
props.description: "transparent" (default) or "filled" (base/250 fill). Figma's Input property is literally named Size, but its two values are fills; it is exposed as fill so it cannot be confused with input-dropdown's width `size`. Sets data-fill. Hover fills either one.

props.name: value
props.description: Current text content. Maps to Penpot's Filled state when non-empty.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when empty, drawn as body text at 50% opacity (Figma). Typed text is full opacity.

props.name: rows
props.description: Only meaningful when type="textarea". Sets the native rows attribute.

rationale: Styled to Figma's Input (node 33:8199 of the application file): a 40px box with a 1px base/400 border and 10px padding, no shadows. Figma's Size property (transparent | filled) is exposed as `fill`. Hover fills the field (base/250) and darkens the border (base/750); focus is a white fill with an accent border, typed text at full opacity. Figma has exactly three states (default, hover, focused) and no disabled, error or pressed state, so none is styled. State is native CSS (:hover, :focus, ::placeholder), no `state` prop. Colors come from the input tokens (--ds-color-input-fill, -border, -border-hover, -border-focus), defined in both themes. The transparent fill has no visible border at rest (Figma D_SYSTEM Inputs card, node 103:4758): the field sits inside something that already frames it, and shows its border on hover and focus, matching input-dropdown; table-cell's notes cell and header-block's search restore the boxed look in their own CSS. width:100% rather than Figma's 280px: that is the swatch's frame, not a component constraint. Not sourced from Figma: type="textarea", which reuses the same box rules without the fixed height. Replaces an earlier Penpot version; its Penpot `source` is kept for traceability. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Native <input type="text">, so labeling is the host page's responsibility (a <label> or aria-label). Focus is shown by the fill turning white and the border turning the accent color (Figma draws no separate outline). The placeholder is 50% opacity body text and is not a substitute for a label.

name: input-dropdown
description: A select-style field: shows the current choice with a dropdown affordance arrow, opens components/dropdown-menu when activated (composed, see index.html — wrap this trigger and a .ds-dropdown-menu together in a .ds-dropdown container). Renamed from Penpot's literal component name "Input_with-icon" — its content is a 'Dropdown' text label plus a chevron, i.e. a select trigger, not a text input with a decorative leading icon.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value shown in the field.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Set when `value` is only a prompt ("Select option"), not a real choice: the label is drawn at 50% opacity like Figma's placeholder text. Sets data-placeholder; component.js removes it when the paired dropdown-menu selects an item.

props.name: fill
props.description: "transparent" (default) or "filled" (base/250 fill). Figma's Input property is named Size but its values are fills; exposed as fill so it stays distinct from the width `size` below. Sets data-fill. Hover fills either one.

props.name: size
props.description: small (140px), middle (300px), or large (100% — fills its container). Sets a fixed width via data-size; the field never grows/shrinks on its own. Not from Penpot — its demo instances were all a single fixed 160px, an artifact of that documentation swatch's own frame size, not a real size system. These three values and their pixel widths were specified directly by the user rather than derived from Penpot (middle started at 240px, widened +60px to 300px on later user request). compact is 200px (a pane head's source dropdown).

rationale: Styled to Figma's Input, Type=text+icon (node 33:8199 of the application file): the same 40px box as `input` (1px base/400 border, 10px padding, no shadows) with the label and a 24px arrow 10px apart. Figma's Size property (transparent | filled) is exposed as `fill`. Hover fills the field (base/250) and darkens the border (base/750); Figma's focused variant (white fill, base/750 border, arrow pointing up) is applied for :focus-visible and for the open menu (aria-expanded), so the arrow shows which way the menu is. Colors come from the input tokens (--ds-color-input-*, plus --ds-color-input-icon for the base/600 arrow). The label is 50% opacity while it is only a prompt and full opacity once a choice is made, so `placeholder` (data-placeholder) is opt-in; component.js clears it on the paired dropdown-menu's ds-dropdown-select event. Renamed from Penpot's "Input_with-icon" because its content is a label plus a chevron, i.e. a select trigger, and the schema's name pattern calls for kebab-case describing behavior. The arrow reuses icons/arrow-down.svg. Figma has only default, hover and focused states, so no disabled or error state is styled. size (small / middle / large) is a fixed-width system not traceable to the design source; data-size="compact" is 200px wide, for a dropdown in a pane head (Figma node 150:16284) -- mirror it onto the .ds-dropdown wrapper so the trigger fills it (see dropdown-menu). Replaces an earlier Penpot version; its `source` is kept for traceability. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Renders as a native <button> (not a real <select>). aria-haspopup="listbox" is set so assistive tech announces it opens a choice list; aria-expanded is toggled automatically by components/dropdown-menu/component.js when this trigger is wrapped in a .ds-dropdown alongside a .ds-dropdown-menu (see index.html). It also still dispatches ds-input-dropdown-open on click/Enter/Space (free via <button>) independent of whether a real menu is attached, for a host page that wants to wire up its own menu instead.

name: loading-veil
description: A dim veil over one area with a small dark "Loading" tooltip: the area under it is loading. Show and hide with the hidden attribute.

props.name: label
props.description: Tooltip text.

props.name: scope
props.description: "page" makes the veil a page's first-load state: fixed, opaque, only the 40px glyph. With data-loading on <html> (set in <head>, removed when data has loaded) every other child of <body> is hidden, then faded in (data-loading-reveal on <html>). Omitted, the veil covers its positioned parent with a "Loading" tooltip.

rationale: The veil covers its positioned parent (inset 0) above the content (z-index 5, below popups at 100 and toasts at 200) with the popup overlay color (bg.overlay) at 50% opacity, exactly like a popup's backdrop, so 'this area is busy' reads the same way as 'this area is behind a dialog'. The tooltip is a dark box (Figma base/900 with a base/1000 hairline, white text, 10px padding and gap) holding the spinner glyph (a CSS mask, so it takes the text color) and the label. It is centered horizontally and translated -50% / -50%, so the host places its center by setting style.top (Figma draws it at the middle of the window, not of the area). Not sourced from Figma: the hidden-attribute API and role="status". Rendering verified in light and dark themes. The spinner rotates clockwise, 1.2s linear per turn, and stops under prefers-reduced-motion. scope="page" is a whole page's first-load state (2026-10-12): opaque veil with the glyph alone at z-index 150, the page's other content hidden through html[data-loading] and faded in on load, with a 10s CSS fail-safe.
a11y_notes: role="status" so the loading message is announced when the veil is shown; the spinner is aria-hidden. The veil does not trap focus: the host should also mark the area inert while loading if it must not be used.

name: nav-bar
description: The primary top navigation bar: a workspace switcher (left), the page / section links (center), and a theme toggle (right). A composition shell, like table-row -- it composes real input-dropdown and text-button instances rather than restyling them. It stays pinned to the top of the viewport while the page scrolls (position:sticky, top:0), with an opaque background and a bottom hairline so it stays legible over scrolling content; this is part of the component, so every page that uses it gets the same behavior.
rationale:
Layout from Penpot's Nav-bar instance: a flex row, centered, justify-content: space-between; both side slots are flex rows too, so buttons of different heights line up. Box values follow the Figma nav instance: 10px (spacing-cell) padding on all four sides and a 0.5px bottom hairline in object-dark-passive -- raw 0.5px because Figma draws it and --ds-border-width-thin (1px) stays correct for tables. Penpot's column gap of 101px is not reproduced: it is an artifact of a fixed 1240px demo board, and with space-between any explicit gap would be right at exactly one width. Sticky, not fixed: the bar is always the page's first full-width element, so both look the same once scrolled, but sticky keeps it in document flow and content below needs no hand-maintained offset. bg.surface and the hairline keep it legible over content scrolling beneath it.

Left: a composed input-dropdown at 160px (the width table-cell's dropdown cell uses for the same Penpot source). Center: text-buttons with no gap (Penpot's gap is 0; the buttons' own padding separates them). Which link is primary (current page) is markup the host supplies; Penpot's "Property 1" axis only changes which link carries it, so it isn't a style variant. Right: the theme toggle is a real text-button (secondary, active, dotted -- toggling stays on the page) with an icon and a visible label ("Dark" / "Light"); both name the target theme, the same convention the site's own toggle uses. The label is not sourced from Penpot, whose theme icon is a bare glyph. The theme icons draw a 16-unit circle in a 24-unit viewBox, so a spacing-7 (24px) box reproduces Penpot's 16px glyph. .ds-nav-bar__theme-* classes are kept only as stable selectors for the toggle script and carry no CSS.

Notification dot: .ds-nav-bar__dot inside a nav link is a 12px accent-2 circle at the link's right edge, toggled with hidden -- an unread-updates marker. It is the only round shape in the system; Figma draws it round. Keeping it in sync across pages is the host's concern. Not sourced from the design: the link click-swap and the theme toggle's behavior, without which the current link would never change and the toggle wouldn't toggle. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: A real <nav aria-label="Primary"> landmark (not in Penpot; a design tool has no landmarks). Center links are <button> elements with aria-current="page" on the current one, updated on click by component.js; in a real site they should be <a href>. The theme toggle's accessible name is its visible label ("Dark" / "Light"), with the icon aria-hidden and no separate aria-label, so visible and accessible names can't diverge (WCAG 2.5.3); both update on every click to name what activating it does. The workspace switcher is input-dropdown as-is; see its notes.

name: page-head
description: The 60px bar under the nav bar of a work page: the page's title and its main action on the left, secondary actions on the right, one hairline underneath.

props.name: title
props.description: Page title (an h1), cut with an ellipsis when it is too long.

props.name: main_action
props.description: Label of the text button next to the title.

props.name: editable
props.description: The title can be clicked to rename it: shows the text cursor and a dotted underline on hover and keyboard focus. The host swaps in the input on click; the component only styles the two states.

props.name: editing
props.description: Render the rename field (.ds-page-head__title-input) in place of the title. Same type tokens, no padding or border, so the bar does not change size.

rationale: Height is spacing.9 + spacing.6 (60px), side padding spacing.6 (20px), bg.surface with one hairline (object-dark.passive) under it. The title is the heading-4 role (Inter SemiBold 20px) with line-height normal, so the bar's height, not the type scale, sets the rhythm. The gap between title and main action is spacing.cell (10px); the right group has no gap because text buttons hug their labels (see text-button). Both groups are flex rows with min-width 0, so a long title ellipsizes instead of pushing the actions out. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Rename in place (2026-10-11): the title is the heading-4 role; the rename field reuses the same four type tokens with zero padding, border and fill, so swapping title for field changes nothing about the box: no jump, no reflow of the actions. It is marked by an accent line drawn as an inset shadow (not a border, which would add height) and sized to its text with field-sizing: content, capped at the bar. The editable title carries the system's dotted-underline clickable affordance on hover and focus only, so a read-only title looks as before. Not from Figma (the Figma bar draws no editing state); built from existing tokens only.
a11y_notes: The title is an h1. The buttons are real text-buttons; keyboard focus uses their own ring. An editable title is focusable (tabindex 0) and the host opens the field on Enter or F2 as well as click; the field has aria-label 'Set name'. Escape cancels and Enter or leaving the field commits, both owned by the host.

name: pane
description: One column of a two-column work area: a 56px head (title and caption at half opacity, optional action button) over a body that scrolls on its own. .ds-split lays panes side by side.

props.name: id
props.description: Prefix of the title's id, used by aria-labelledby.

props.name: title
props.description: Pane title.

props.name: caption
props.description: Caption next to the title (a count, a page count).

props.name: action
props.description: Label of the head's text button.

rationale:
Head height is spacing.9 + spacing.5 (56px), side padding spacing.6, bg.surface, one hairline under it. The title uses the "title" role (Inter SemiBold 16px) and the caption the caption role (Inter Italic 16px), both at 50% opacity as in Figma, bottom-aligned so their baselines meet, spacing.cell apart. .ds-pane__body and .ds-pane__scroll are separate so a positioned body (e.g. one a loading-veil covers) can wrap the scrolling region, while a simple pane scrolls directly under the head. The scrollbar is hidden (scrollbar-width: none); wheel, keys and touch still scroll.

Attributes: data-divider="start" on the head and body draws a hairline on the pane's left edge (the divider between two panes); data-emphasis="true" on the title shows it at full opacity; a body with the hidden attribute is hidden (tab panels).

Resizable split: any flex row with data-resizable and a .ds-split__handle between two neighbours. The handle is a 0-wide flex item on the border between them, with an 8px (spacing.3) grab area centered on the line and a 2px accent line on hover, focus and while dragging. Dragging, or ArrowLeft / ArrowRight (24px a step), resizes the target: data-resize-target="end" (default) the element after the handle, "start" the one before it. data-min-size / data-min-rest set the target's and the rest's minimum in pixels (default 320 each). The size is applied as data-resized plus --_resize-size on the target, not an inline flex, so CSS states keep priority (sidebar-list's collapsed rule beats it, and the handle beside a collapsed sidebar is hidden). data-resize-key remembers the target's share of the row in localStorage (a share, so another window width keeps the proportion; missing or failing storage just starts equal). It emits ds-split-resize and a window resize, so nested splits re-apply their stored share and paper-preview's scroll thumb updates. Not sourced from Figma: the handle and resizing; the design shows only the divider line. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: The pane is a <section>; label it with aria-labelledby pointing at the title. The head button is a real text-button. The resize handle is role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical", focusable, with aria-valuenow/min/max as the end pane's share of the split in percent; give it an aria-label naming what it resizes.

name: paper-preview
description: A page preview shell for document-style cards (templates, collections), composed with skeleton placeholder content rather than real copy. Two modes: one-longread (a single continuous sheet, text placeholder only) and paged-preview (several A4 sheets stacked with gaps, scrollable inline, text and image placeholders). Each mode supports portrait and landscape.

props.name: mode
props.description: Sets data-mode. "one-longread" (default) renders a single continuous page with no gap/scroll behavior -- generalizes Penpot's real Template/Draft pattern (one board, no page split). "paged-preview" renders several .ds-paper-preview__page children stacked with an 8px gap inside a fixed-height, vertically-scrollable frame -- generalizes Penpot's real Collection/Template-Visual pattern (several Page-N boards in a flex column).

props.name: orientation
props.description: Sets data-orientation, which controls each sheet's aspect-ratio: "portrait" is 538:761, "landscape" 761:538 -- both true A4 (1:sqrt(2)), pixel-matched to Penpot's A4-proportioned Page-N boards and their transpose. The card stretches to 100% of its container's width; sheets scale with it.

rationale:
Generalizes the two structural patterns of Penpot's "Paper-Cards" board into a blank, reusable shell (Penpot has no paper-preview component): one-longread is a single uninterrupted sheet; paged-preview is several sheets in a column with a spacing.3 (8px) gap, Token-bound in Penpot and confirmed by measured positions. The container is bg.surface with no padding, so it shows only in the gaps between sheets. Sheets are true A4 (1:sqrt(2)): landscape 761:538, pixel-matched to Penpot's one A4-proportioned instance, portrait its transpose. Sheets are width:100% with aspect-ratio, so the proportion holds at any container width. In light, a sheet is white (Figma base/0); a picture inside a sheet fills its box (object-fit: cover). No shadow, border or radius: none of the sourced instances has any, so a flat rectangle is the actual sourced look.

paged-preview scrolls inline within a fixed max-height of 500px (a viewport constraint, not a token; vh would break inside the auto-resizing iframe the site embeds demos in). The native scrollbar is hidden and replaced by an overlay thumb, the same technique gallery uses horizontally: it shows only while scrolling and fades out after, and as an absolutely positioned overlay it never shifts content. Placeholder bars reuse gallery-image's skeleton convention (object-white.disabled bars, spacing-2 within a stack, spacing-6 between sections); the image placeholder reuses gallery-image's object-dark-passive stand-in at 16:9. .ds-paper-preview-stack is the scrolling column of sheets used inside a pane. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: A visual placeholder shell: the skeleton bars and rectangles stand in for content that doesn't exist yet, so they carry no role or label. A host rendering real document content into the sheets adds the real structure at that point (headings, landmarks, alt text). The scrollable frame is a plain overflow:auto <div> with no tabindex or role="region", since an empty region would be a false affordance; add both once real content is composed in. The custom scrollbar is aria-hidden and pointer-events:none -- a visual echo of native scrolling, not a control.

name: popup
description: A modal panel: a title, a body (free text, a single input field, or a gallery + text-icon selector), and a bottom action row of one or two buttons, shown over a real full-viewport dimmed backdrop that a trigger button opens and the bottom row's own buttons (or Escape/backdrop click) close. No close/X control -- dismissal is via the bottom row's own buttons.

props.name: type
props.description: Sets data-type on .ds-popup__body. "text" renders free paragraphs (Penpot's "Summary"); "input" composes a real .ds-input field (Penpot's "Description"); "gallery" composes a real gallery filmstrip plus a gallery-image type="text-icon" selector -- a smaller answer to Penpot's "Image-sliders", see rationale.

props.name: size
props.description: small (500px, Figma's confirmations), medium (800px, Add Description and Summary), or large (1200px, not from a Figma frame yet). Sets data-size on .ds-popup.

props.name: placement
props.description: "center" (default: centered over a full-viewport backdrop dimmed 50%) or "anchored" (a confirmation: 10px under the trigger that opened it, at least 20px from the viewport edge, backdrop dimmed 30% -- see component.js's positionAnchored() and style.css). Sets data-placement on .ds-popup-overlay.

props.name: preview
props.description: inline: render the popup open, in the page flow (backdrop included), without the hidden attribute -- data-preview="inline". Documentation only (the site's Popups card, Figma D_SYSTEM node 103:4815); never in product UI.

props.name: closable
props.description: Adds a close icon (an X, 24px) at the right edge of the title row. It carries data-popup-dismiss, so it closes the popup like any dismiss button.

rationale:
Styled to Figma's popup-medium (application file, nodes 150:16627, 150:16661, 150:16695, 150:16729), superseding the earlier Penpot values. The panel is bg.surface with no shadow: the dimmed backdrop is what sets it off the page. Title, body and bottom row share one surface with no dividers (as in both design sources), so the panel reads as one plain stack. The title row is 60px with the heading role (heading-4, Inter SemiBold 20). The body has 20px side and 10px vertical padding and scrolls once the panel reaches the viewport; data-type="steps" drops the padding for stacked popup-step sections that carry their own insets. The bottom row is 60px with the actions right-aligned 10px apart; text-button's brackets hang inside each button's 11px padding, so a button is exactly its label plus padding. There is no close (X) control: the design has none, and the bottom row's buttons (plus Escape and a backdrop click) dismiss. Figma's caption slot beside the title and its hidden header action are opacity 0 in every frame and are not modeled.

Sizes: medium 800px (Penpot's panel width; a modal's width is a design decision, not container-driven), small 500px (Figma's confirmation width), large 1173px (Figma's Add project frame, nodes 150:16503 / 150:16475). Backdrop (measured off the design's screens): base/600 gray at 50% behind a centered popup and 30% behind an anchored confirmation. It is a translucent ::before layer, not opacity on the overlay, which would also fade the panel. placement="anchored" sits 10px under its trigger (spacing-3 + spacing-1), never closer than 20px (spacing-6) to a viewport edge, flips above the trigger when it would overflow, and caps its height to the viewport -- measured against documentElement.clientWidth/Height, so a scrollbar gutter doesn't push it past the visible edge.

Body types: "text" (free paragraphs), "input" (Figma's filled textarea, 300px tall in a 320px row), and "gallery" -- a composed gallery filmstrip plus a gallery-image text-icon selector, with a "Reset selection" text-button wired through gallery's generic data-gallery-reset contract, so popup has no gallery-specific code. "gallery" is a deliberately smaller answer to Penpot's "Image-sliders" instance, which nests several sub-widgets that aren't built components.

Behavior (component.js; not sourced -- a design tool doesn't model opening a dialog): a [data-popup-open] trigger shows the matching overlay; any bottom-row button with [data-popup-dismiss] closes it, as do Escape and a backdrop click; both are delegated listeners, so buttons added later work too. Focus moves to the panel on open and back to the trigger on close. Overlays stack: a popup opened from inside another gets a z-index 10 higher (base 100, above dropdown-menu), and Escape and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter act only on the topmost. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter presses the bottom-row action marked data-popup-confirm (template: confirm: true), else a priority=primary one -- every Figma action is a regular-weight secondary button, so primary can't be the only signal. A destructive action (e.g. "Archive selected") uses text-button's error status. Triggers and dismiss buttons are dotted: opening or closing a modal stays in the view. The anchored rule is scoped :not([hidden]) so it never overrides the hidden state. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Scroll lock (explicit request 2026-10-11): while any overlay is open, <html> carries data-popup-scroll-lock and does not scroll, so the wheel moves only the popup body; the native scrollbar width is put back as padding to avoid a sideways shift, and overscroll-behavior: contain stops chaining. It is set from the same stack that stacks overlays, so it clears only when the last one closes.
a11y_notes: role="dialog" with aria-labelledby pointing at its title (not in the design source). Implemented: showing and hiding, Escape and backdrop click to close, focus onto the dialog on open and back to the opener on close (also when popups are nested), and Escape / Ctrl+Enter acting only on the topmost popup. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter clicks the confirm button directly, so it is exactly as accessible as clicking it. Tab / Shift+Tab are trapped in the topmost open popup (2026-10-03): Tab from the last focusable control wraps to the first, Shift+Tab from the first or from the panel wraps to the last, and focus outside the popup is pulled back in. The panel keeps a keyboard-only focus ring although Figma draws none. type="gallery" inherits gallery's and gallery-image's own semantics (see their notes). The optional close icon is a real <button aria-label="Close"> outside the title element, so the dialog name stays the title.

name: popup-step
description: One numbered step of a long popup body: a 56px head (numbered title at half opacity, optional text button) over a body that holds the step's control.

props.name: number
props.description: The step's number (the <ol start> value).

props.name: title
props.description: Step title.

props.name: action
props.description: Label of the head's text button (e.g. Reset the selection); omitted when absent.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Makes the step an accordion section: clicking the head (or Enter / Space on the title) shows or hides the body.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: With collapsible: the step starts closed.

rationale: The head is 56px (spacing.9 + spacing.5) with 20px side padding, no border and no fill: the popup surface shows through, and steps are separated by their own heads, not by rules. The title is an ordered list with start=N and one item, so the number is real list numbering; the 24px inline-start margin (spacing.7) makes room for it, and the title uses the "title" role at half opacity, like a pane title. The body is inset spacing.cell (10px) / spacing.6 (20px). A .ds-dropdown directly inside a step fills the width. The head's text button hugs its label (see text-button). Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Collapsible (2026-10-12): the head toggles the body that follows it (data-collapsed on the head, so markup stays two siblings); the body animates height over 150ms and is hidden from focus and assistive tech when closed; the open step's title goes to full opacity. window.dsPopupStep.setOpen() lets a host open or close steps from code.
a11y_notes: Each title is an <ol> with a single <li> so screen readers announce the step number. The head button is a real text-button. Collapsible steps: the title's <li> becomes role=button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, reachable by Tab, toggled by Enter / Space; a closed body is visibility:hidden.

name: radio
description: A radio option drawn as a text button with a round Figma marker (ring in the accent color, filled when checked). Compose several in a .ds-radio-group.

props.name: options
props.description: Each option: { value, label, checked }.

props.name: label
props.description: aria-label of the radiogroup.

rationale: An option is a real .ds-text-button with role=radio, so it keeps the text button's type, underline and focus ring. The marker is CSS only: a ring spacing.8 / 2 (16px) in the accent color drawn with an inset shadow, and a spacing.9 / 4 (10px) dot when aria-checked is true, centered in a 24px (spacing.7) box. The text button's hover "[ ]" is removed (content: none) because the marker already shows which option is under the pointer. Height is spacing.9 (40px); options stack with a spacing.cell (10px) gap. Not sourced from Figma: the roving tabindex and arrow-key behavior in component.js. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: role="radiogroup" with role="radio" options and aria-checked. Only the checked option is in the tab order (roving tabindex); arrow keys move and check.

name: sidebar-item
description: One entry in a sidebar list (sidebar-list composes several). type="set": one row of a sets sidebar (a clickable name, optional save toggle). type="card": a subtitle, a saved-icon, a title and a status line. type="button": a single primary action. Renamed from Penpot's "Sidebar" to avoid colliding with the composed list, which this system names sidebar-list.

props.name: type
props.description: "card" renders the subtitle/title/status card (Penpot's Default/PDF Downloaded/Submitted States -- identical layout, only the status text differs, so not modeled as three separate types); "button" renders a single centered .ds-text-button instead (Penpot's own "Button" State) -- not a card at all. "set" (not from Penpot, see rationale) renders a clickable set-name button + toggleable save icon on one row, one caption line below.

props.name: name
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". The set's name, rendered as a clickable secondary text-button (selects the set), truncated with an ellipsis when it overflows.

props.name: caption
props.description: type="set": optional second line under the name, in grey (text-active at half opacity, the same grey as table-cell's text-passive-cell) -- e.g. a record's status. The row grows to two lines; without it the set row stays the single 44px line. (Kept from the earlier Penpot set card; shown again since 2026-09-30.)

props.name: saved
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". Initial data-saved state for the save icon; component.js keeps it in sync on click and dispatches ds-sidebar-item-favourite-toggle.

props.name: active
props.description: type="set": marks the active set (fill and hairlines above and below).

props.name: muted
props.description: type="set": a record that needs no more action (e.g. an application already sent). Its name is grey at rest and takes the accent back on hover, focus, or when active.

props.name: href
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". When given, the set name renders as an <a href> (still the same secondary/dotted text-button) instead of a <button data-select-set> -- for a sidebar whose rows navigate, e.g. an in-page section index (dotted, because it stays on the page; CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). Passed through the safe_url filter.

props.name: save
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". false omits the save button entirely (a navigation row has nothing to save). Default true.

rationale:
type="set" (Figma sets sidebar): a 44px row with the set's name as a text button and a 44px save button with Figma's bookmark icons (aria-pressed toggles them); the active set (data-active) is filled and ruled above and below, and its name uses the body-text medium weight, so the current set stands out without a new type scale. The saved icon is accent-1, the same as table-cell's row-level favourite: one save flag, one color, wherever it renders. With `href`, the name renders as an <a> (navigation, e.g. an in-page section index) instead of a <button>, and save=false omits the save button; one row layout serves both uses. Rows deviate from text-button's hover brackets: on hover and focus the whole row takes bg.surface-pressed, as table-row does, and the name gets no brackets -- the full-width fill already marks the click target. The dotted underline stays. A long name truncates with an ellipsis (the composed text button can shrink: flex 1 1 auto, min-width 0).

type="card" and type="button" (Penpot "Sidebar" states Default, PDF Downloaded, Submitted, Button): the main section is a space-between row and the sub section a column with rowGap spacing-3, both Token-bound in Penpot. Card padding is spacing-2 / spacing-5. Colors are read off the text layers: subtitle accent-1 (the one colored identifier a reader scans the list for), title text-active, status text-subactive. The saved icon is object-dark-active at spacing-7 (24px), like every other icon-only glyph. Width is 100%, because a sidebar's width comes from its container, not from Penpot's 340px demo board. type="button" is shorter (70px vs 84px) and centered, holding one primary text-button, as Penpot's own instance is. Selecting, linking or adding records is the host application's concern. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Set rows follow Figma D_SYSTEM 28:1718 (default), 28:1721 (hover: base/100 fill with base/300 hairlines) and 188:4543 (selected: base/150 fill in light, black Medium name without underline, hairlines). Added 2026-10-12.
a11y_notes: type="set": the name is a real <button> (or <a> with href; the active row gets aria-current), and the save control is a real <button> with aria-pressed and an aria-label naming the set, so both are keyboard-operable. type="card": the saved-icon is a decorative role="img" span with an aria-label, not a control -- the design shows no affordance on it. type="button" is a real <button> via text-button.

name: sidebar-list
description: A sets sidebar: a 280px column with a 60px head (title, collapse toggle) over a scrolling list of sidebar-item type="set" rows, optionally opened by a 56px create row. Collapses to a 64px strip.

props.name: title
props.description: Head title, shown at half opacity.

props.name: create
props.description: Label of the create row, the first item of the list (a primary text-button in a type="set" sidebar-item with data-role="create"). Omit for none. Its height is the pane heads' (56px), so it lines up with them.

props.name: label
props.description: aria-label of the sidebar.

props.name: items
props.description: Set rows: { name, saved, active, href?, save? } -- href/save pass through to sidebar-item type="set" (see its meta.json): href makes the row a link, save=false drops its save button.

rationale: Width is spacing.9 x 7 (280px), collapsed spacing.row + 2 x spacing.cell (64px). The head is 60px (spacing.9 + spacing.6, changed from 56px on 2026-10-11 so it lines up with the page head beside it) with 10px padding and one hairline below; the optional create row is 56px (spacing.9 + spacing.5, the pane head's height) and every other row keeps the sidebar-item height; the title is the "title" role (Inter SemiBold 16px) at half opacity; the toggle is a 44 x 40px bordered button holding the accent-colored arrow (a CSS mask, so it takes the accent color), flipped when collapsed. The list has no rules between rows: only the active set is ruled, inside sidebar-item, so the one row that matters stands out. Surface is bg.surface with a right hairline in object-dark.passive in both themes (the design has no separate dark value yet). Collapse behavior and its ARIA state live in component.js; choosing and saving sets is the host page's concern (sidebar-item exposes data-select-set / data-save-set hooks). Replaces an earlier Penpot card sidebar. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Collapsed (updated 2026-10-12): the sidebar stays a 64px strip in the page flow; the toggle slides the full panel open over the page (clip-path 200ms, data-peek) without moving the layout, and a click outside, Escape or choosing a row closes it. The create row follows Figma D_SYSTEM 28:1729: 45px, bold dotted-underlined name, a plus in the icon cell, a closing hairline.
a11y_notes: An <aside> with aria-label. The toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and a label that flips between Collapse sidebar and Expand sidebar; each set row's name and save buttons are real buttons (the save button uses aria-pressed).

name: table-cell
description: A single cell within a table-row of a queue table: text data, an icon/checkbox slot, a link, a dropdown/input field, or an action-button slot, depending on `type`. table-row composes several of these per row; header-block's divider marks the boundary between the header and the first row of cells.

props.name: type
props.description: Which cell kind this renders: checkbox-cell (was Penpot's "icon"), icon-cell (was "saved" and "action-icons", merged into one type that holds any number of icons), date, text-active-cell (was "title", "organisation" and "description", already identical), text-passive-cell (was "source"), text-subactive-cell (was "summary"), link, 1-action, 2-actions, 3-actions, dropdown, input, empty-state, status-label. See rationale.

props.name: content
props.description: The cell's text content, for text-bearing types (date, text-active-cell, text-passive-cell, text-subactive-cell, link, dropdown, input). Not applicable to checkbox-cell, icon-cell, 1-action, 2-actions, 3-actions, or empty-state, which have fixed or composed content. For 1-action/2-actions/3-actions, doubles as the primary (rightmost) button's label.

props.name: checkbox_role
props.description: Only meaningful when type="checkbox-cell". Unset (default): the normal row-select checkbox (unchecked / checked), toggled by table-row off the row's data-selected. "select-all": adds a third icon (checkbox-semi-select) and marks the cell data-checkbox-role="select-all", so table-row's select-all logic and table-cell's [data-state] rules can target it. Not sourced from the design.

props.name: editable
props.description: Text-bearing types only (not checkbox-cell/icon-cell/dropdown/input/1-action/2-actions/3-actions/empty-state/status-label). Renders a hidden .ds-input sibling alongside the text span and marks the cell data-editable so a same-row [data-edit-trigger] button (see extra_attrs) can toggle it into edit mode -- see component.js.

props.name: extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="1-action" (and as the primary button's attrs for "2-actions"/"3-actions"). Raw attribute string passed through to the composed text-button's own extra_attrs passthrough (see text-button/template.html) -- e.g. extra_attrs='data-edit-trigger' to wire an Edit button at a row's own editable cell, the same pattern popup already uses for data-popup-open/dismiss.

props.name: secondary_extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="2-actions"/"3-actions". Same passthrough as extra_attrs, but for the secondary (middle, Dismiss-style) button instead of the primary one.

props.name: tertiary_label
props.description: Only meaningful for type="3-actions". Label for the leftmost, lowest-emphasis of the 3 buttons (secondary priority, same as the middle button).

props.name: tertiary_extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="3-actions". Same passthrough as extra_attrs/secondary_extra_attrs, but for the tertiary (leftmost) button.

props.name: options
props.description: Only meaningful when type="dropdown". A list of { value, label }: when given, the input-dropdown trigger is wired (data-dropdown-trigger) inside a .ds-dropdown wrapper with a dropdown-menu of these items, so the cell's dropdown actually opens (link components/dropdown-menu's component.js on the page). Omitted: the unwired trigger alone, unchanged.

props.name: dropdown_label
props.description: Only meaningful with options. The trigger's aria-label (the visible text is the current value, not what the control is for).

props.name: view_label
props.description: Text-bearing types only. Renders Figma's "Single-active-t+button" cell (D_SYSTEM node 28:949): the text clipped to one line with an ellipsis, followed by a secondary dotted text-button with this label (e.g. "view") that stays whole. The host page wires the button (e.g. to a popup showing the full text).

rationale:
Layout (Figma flat table): every cell is one table row high -- spacing.row (44px) plus a 1px object-dark-passive hairline under it -- with spacing.cell (10px) padding, on bg.surface, and no vertical rules. Text is one line with an ellipsis; .ds-table-cell__clip clips an excerpt beside an inline "view" button. Cells share the row's width (flex 1 1 0%); fixed-content types (checkbox-cell, icon-cell, input, the action types, status-label) are flex: none and size to their content. Link cells right-align and never wrap (at most two lines, accent-1, underline on hover). Action cells left-align with a 16px right padding. A dropdown or input cell lets its field fill the cell; the input keeps its box border in the cell (Figma's table rows draw it), although input's transparent fill is borderless elsewhere.

Types: started as Penpot's 15 Type values and were merged where Penpot's own cells were identical. text-active-cell (was title / organisation / description -- pixel-identical in Penpot) is text.active body text; text-passive-cell (was source) and text-subactive-cell (was summary; body-text italic) keep Penpot's identifiers; icon-cell (was saved and action-icons) holds any number of icons, adopting action-icons' multi-icon layout, a deliberate deviation for a lone saved icon; checkbox-cell (was icon) is Penpot's generic single-icon cell, also used for the drag handle. Penpot's State axis is "Value 1" (an unused placeholder) on almost every type, so there is no `state` prop: hover lives in the composed controls. Composition, not restyling: action cells compose text-button, dropdown and input cells compose input-dropdown and input.

Icons: every glyph is the Figma D_SYSTEM set (node 103:4711) in icons/, inlined by component.js so currentColor and --_icon-fill / --_icon-mark apply. Checkbox and save rest as an input-icon outline on an input-fill box (input-icon rather than Figma's text-inactive, which disappears on the dark surface) and turn accent on hover; a selected checkbox is an accent box with an inverse mark; a saved bookmark fills with accent-2. checkbox-cell carries both an unchecked and a checked icon, and table-row's CSS swaps them off the row's data-selected, so selection needs no extra script. The checkbox styling is scoped to [data-icon="checkbox"], so a drag glyph in the same cell layout isn't recolored; data-icon="drag" paints Figma's drag glyph.

Row actions: in light, active action buttons rest in text-inactive (like an inactive tab title) and turn accent-1 while their row is hovered, focused or selected (Figma node 237:31166), so a long table isn't a wall of blue; disabled, loading, error and unread buttons keep their own color. Dark keeps them accent, because dark's text-inactive would not read on its background. 1-action, 2-actions and 3-actions share one shape (row, left-aligned, flex: none); 3-actions has no Penpot instance and follows 2-actions.

Additions not sourced from the design: `editable` renders the text and a hidden .ds-input side by side and toggles hidden, so the cell's size never changes between states; the trigger is a row's own button (extra_attrs='data-edit-trigger'), because editing sits behind an explicit action. extra_attrs / secondary_extra_attrs / tertiary_extra_attrs pass raw attributes through to the composed text-buttons (author markup, never user data). status-label is a plain, non-interactive span in system-success replacing an action group once a record is done -- not a disabled button, since there is nothing to click. `checkbox_role="select-all"` adds a third, semi-selected icon for a header checkbox that table-row drives. Shift+click on a Save icon saves or unsaves the range since the last Save click in the same table (visible rows, DOM order), dispatched as one ds-table-cell-favourite-toggle event with detail.range = true. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Collapsed excerpt (explicit request 2026-10-11): a text cell is an ellipsized excerpt (.ds-table-cell__clip) followed by a text button, usually "view". A button carrying data-collapse-label opts in: when the column leaves room for ten characters of the excerpt or fewer (measured with the excerpt's real font, re-measured on every width change and for cells added later), component.js sets data-collapsed on the .ds-table-cell__text, style.css hides the excerpt, and the button is renamed after the field ("Summary", "Full Description") and lines up like a button standing in for column text. Other cells are untouched. The threshold is a constant in component.js because it is a behavior, not a style value.
a11y_notes: type="dropdown" renders a real .ds-input-dropdown <button> (listen for its ds-input-dropdown-open event); type="input" a real <input type="text">; type="link" a real <a href>. Icon cells use role="img" with an aria-label per icon, since each icon is its own unit; the inlined SVGs carry no separate text. Icons are fetched at runtime relative to the script's own URL (so they work wherever the system is vendored), and need http(s): from file:// the icon slots stay empty. Known gaps: the Save icon toggles on click but stays role="img" with no aria-pressed and no keyboard handler, so its state isn't announced and it is pointer-only, as is Shift+click range saving; `editable`'s switch to the input moves focus but isn't announced, and the input has no label. status-label is plain text.

name: table-footer
description: The row under a table's last row that loads more of it ("Load 10 more", "Load all 100"): a 44px row on the pressed surface whose first button aligns with the third column's text.

props.name: first_label
props.description: Label of the first (text-aligned) button.

props.name: second_label
props.description: Label of the second button.

props.name: first_action
props.description: data-action value of the first button, for the host page to listen for.

props.name: second_action
props.description: data-action value of the second button.

rationale: Height is one table row: spacing.row (44px) plus the 1px hairline, like every table row. Fill is bg.surface-pressed (Figma base/100). The hairline is border.muted (base/150), with object-dark.passive as the fallback because border.muted has no dark value yet. Left padding is two 44px icon columns plus the 10px cell padding, so the first button's label starts where the Name column's text starts: the first button is a text-aligned button (no left padding, hover "[" hung outside the label), exactly like table-cell's text-active-cell button. Not sourced from Figma: the data-action hooks, through which the host page attaches its own load behavior; no behavior lives in the component. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Two real <button> elements; keyboard focus uses text-button's own focus ring. The row has no landmark role: it is part of the table's section.

name: table-header
description: The title region of a table's header-block: either a single section title, a two-tab selector (e.g. switching between status views), or a title paired with a secondary info caption (e.g. page count). Sits to the left of table-header-actions inside header-block. Standalone, it renders as its own shaded/bordered chip (see rationale); nested inside header-block, that chip is reset to plain, since header-block's own row now carries the same shading across its full width instead (see components/header-block/meta.json).

props.name: type
props.description: 1-tab (single title), 2-tabs (two clickable labels, one active/one inactive), or title-info (title + subactive caption). Maps to Penpot's `type` variant axis; Penpot's own values were kebab-cased ("1 Tab" -> "1-tab", etc.).

rationale:
All three variants share two Token-bound values from Penpot's instances: a left inset of spacing.6 (20px) and, when there is a second element, a column gap of spacing.5 (16px). Title and tab labels use the heading-4 role; the component never uses bold heading weights. type="2-tabs" encodes selection with color alone: the selected tab is text.active, the other text.inactive -- the system's existing active/inactive vocabulary.
