Clicking is wired in component.js because an active/inactive pair with no way to switch would be a dead affordance; the static design source doesn't model the click. type="title-info" pairs the title with a bodyText caption in text.subactive, the token for de-emphasized but legible secondary text (e.g. "3 pages"). An optional `info` caption on 2-tabs (not sourced from Penpot) reuses the same caption styling, for a count under the tabs; without `info`, 2-tabs renders unchanged.

Standalone, the component is a shaded chip: bg.surface-pressed with the border-width-thin / object-dark-passive border table-cell's grid uses, so it reads as part of the same bordered table. This is a deliberate deviation from Penpot, whose instances carry no background or border, modeled on a wikitable caption. bg.surface-pressed was chosen because it moves in the theme-appropriate emphasis direction in both palettes. Sizing stays content-hugging, because the component is a flex child of header-block's row next to table-header-actions. Inside header-block, the row itself carries the shading across its full width, so header-block/style.css resets this chip's background, border and padding there to avoid a doubled box. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: type="2 Tabs" renders as role="tablist" with role="tab"/aria-selected on each label per WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, since Penpot's design implies exactly that interaction (one selected, one not, click to switch). type="1-tab" and "title-info" render as plain text (no tab semantics, since there's nothing to select between). The new optional caption on "2-tabs" is a plain <span>, outside the tablist's own role semantics (a caption describing table contents, not a third tab).

name: table-header-actions
description: The action-button cluster docked at the right side of a table's header-block (e.g. "Add item", "Export", "Clear filters"). A row of 1-4 text-button instances, ordered from least to most emphasis with the single primary action always last/rightmost. Renamed from Penpot's literal component name "table-header_right-block" (see rationale).
rationale: Renamed from Penpot's "table-header_right-block": the schema's name pattern rejects the underscore. Penpot's Actions axis values ("1 Action" ... "3 Actions", and inconsistently "4") are normalized to "1-action" ... "4-actions". The component is only a flex-row shell: column gap 0 (Token-confirmed in Penpot -- the buttons' own padding separates them) and right padding 0, because header-block's row already carries the 20px side padding and the buttons hug their labels. It composes real text-button instances rather than restyling buttons, because Penpot's source is itself composition: every child in every sampled instance is a text-button (no fill token, only a label). The emphasis pattern read off the instances: each extra action is lower emphasis, and the single primary action is always last, rightmost. Every sampled action (Add item, Export, Clear filters, Select all) acts within the current table view, so all use the dotted underline (CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). Each action may carry a `status` (text-button's, default 'active'), so bulk actions can render disabled until rows are selected. It sets no background, so header-block's shaded row shows through behind its buttons. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.

name: table-header-cell
description: A single column-header cell for a table's header row: a plain label, a sort button with a direction arrow when the column is sortable, and/or a favourite-all toggle for a Save column. Sibling cells sharing one [data-sort-group] container sort exclusively -- only one column at a time.

props.name: sortable
props.description: When true, renders the label inside a clickable sort button with a direction-arrow icon. When false, renders a plain, non-interactive label (unless favourite_all is also set).

props.name: label
props.description: The column's header text.

props.name: sort_dir
props.description: Initial data-sort-dir: none, asc, or desc. Only meaningful when sortable=true.

props.name: favourite_all
props.description: For a Save column's header cell: adds a favourite-all toggle beside the sort button -- two independent click targets, the icon toggles every row's saved state and the arrow sorts by it. Sets data-favourite-all / data-type="icon-cell" on the cell so table-row's updateFavouriteAllState() and table-cell's favourite listener drive it (see rationale).

props.name: all_saved
props.description: Initial data-saved state for the favourite-all button. Only meaningful when favourite_all=true; table-row/component.js's updateFavouriteAllState() keeps it in sync at runtime once rows exist.

props.name: filter
props.description: Renders the label as a button that opens a dropdown-menu of values, for a column whose rows can be narrowed to one value. Sets data-filter / data-filter-value on the cell. Takes precedence over sortable. The page needs dropdown-menu's style.css and component.js as well.

props.name: filter_options
props.description: The values after the first item, each { value, label }. Only meaningful when filter=true. With filter_multiple, an option with selected=false starts unticked (every other one starts ticked).

props.name: filter_all_label
props.description: Label of the first item, whose value is "" and which clears the filter. Only meaningful when filter=true.

props.name: filter_icon
props.description: Only meaningful when filter=true. The icons/<name>.svg glyph beside the label: "arrow" (default) or "filter" -- Figma D_SYSTEM's filter glyph (node 38:2934), which its All table uses on a filterable column header.

props.name: filter_multiple
props.description: Only meaningful when filter=true. The menu is dropdown-menu's checkbox list (multiple=true), so several values show at once; the first item (filter_all_label) ticks or clears all. Sets data-filter-multiple and data-filter-values (the ticked values, space-separated) on the cell; ds-table-header-cell-filter carries { values }.

rationale:
Not built from a design-source instance: neither Penpot nor Figma had a column header with a sort affordance when it was built. It generalizes a working pattern from this repo's earlier sample table (site.css / site.js); every visual value was already token-bound there. Styled since to Figma's header cell (Table cell, header-cell text+icon: default 35:8275, hovered 35:8396, selected 35:8423) and the flat table: 44px plus a 1px hairline like a row. Labels use the "data" role (Inter Medium 13px, uppercase) in both themes -- type doesn't depend on the theme -- in the header-cell-label token (base/600) in light and text-subactive in dark.

Sortable: default is the header gray on the plain cell; hovered is black on base/100; selected -- the column with data-sort-dir asc or desc -- is the accent color on base/100, label and arrow always sharing one color. The label keeps its dotted underline (sorting stays in the view) and the 24px arrow (icons/arrow-down.svg) stays visible in every state, 10px from the label. The sort and favourite-all buttons carry the 10px cell padding, so the whole cell is clickable. Siblings in one [data-sort-group] sort exclusively. The component doesn't reorder rows: it cycles data-sort-dir and dispatches a bubbling event, and the host sorts its own rows -- a reusable header can't know the host table's row shape.

favourite_all: a Save column's header needs two independent click targets in one cell -- the icon toggles every row's saved state, a separate arrow sorts by it. The cell carries data-favourite-all and data-type="icon-cell" so table-row's updateFavouriteAllState() and table-cell's favourite listener drive it; the icon markup is hand-matched to table-cell's icon-cell (a nested .ds-table-cell would draw a doubled box), so it isn't declared in `uses`, and the icon-cell padding it picks up is reset for the header layout.

Filter (no design-source node): a header cell whose label opens a dropdown-menu of values. It reuses the sortable header's three states (selected = a value is chosen or the menu is open) and the 24px arrow, or Figma D_SYSTEM's filter glyph (node 38:2934) with filter_icon="filter". The label keeps the column's name. The component records the choice (data-filter-value, accent state, aria-selected) and dispatches ds-table-header-cell-filter with {value, label}; the host narrows its rows. The dropdown wrapper and menu markup are hand-matched, so dropdown-menu isn't in `uses` and a host links its CSS and JS itself. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Filter, multiple (explicit request 2026-10-01: a Status column that shows several statuses at once, all but Archived and Filtered by default): the same header button, with dropdown-menu's checkbox list (included, so the item markup has one source). Its "All" item is ticked when every value is and half-ticked when only some are; the button is accent while any value is left out, the same "this column is filtered" state as the single filter. Column resize (explicit request 2026-10-01, no design source): opt-in with data-column-resize on the grid container (its value a localStorage key, "ds-columns:<key>"). Each header cell but the last column gets pane's split handle on its right edge (8px grab area inside the cell, 2px accent line on hover, focus and drag). Dragging moves a column's right border and the columns after it share the difference in proportion (none under the minimum), so the table keeps its width and the columns to the left stay put; arrow keys move it 24px, a double click restores the CSS widths. Sizes are applied as data-columns-resized + --_column-sizes (minmax(0, <px>fr) per column, so a resized table keeps its proportions at another window width), never under spacing.9, and a column marked data-resize-min="content" (on its header cell or a wrapper around it) never under what its content needs: measured at the start of each drag by laying the grid out once with those columns at max-content, and kept as the track's CSS floor (minmax(max-content, ...)) so content that grows later still fits (explicit request 2026-10-01: buttons, a checkbox or a status never squeezed until they no longer fit); cells in a resized table drop their min-width so a column can be narrower than its content. Each drag, arrow step or reset fires ds-table-columns-resize { before, after } (px, or null for the CSS widths) and the container takes ds-table-columns-set { sizes } back, so a host can undo a resize (the consuming app's Ctrl+Z).
a11y_notes: The sort button is a native <button> with an aria-label ("Sort by <label>") stating the action; the direction is in data-sort-dir and not announced separately -- a host using a real <table> could add aria-sort on the header cell (the component assumes a CSS grid of divs, like table-row). Filter: the trigger is a native <button> with aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-expanded kept by dropdown-menu, and an aria-label naming the column and, once chosen, the value ("Filter by Type: Analysed"); the menu is a role="listbox" of role="option" buttons with aria-selected on the chosen one. Escape and an outside click close it. Filter, multiple: the menu is aria-multiselectable; aria-label lists the shown values while some are left out ("Filter by Status: For review, Analysed"). Column resize: each handle is a focusable role="separator" (aria-orientation vertical, aria-label "Resize <label>"); ArrowLeft / ArrowRight move the border 24px.

name: table-preview
description: Every table type of the Figma D_SYSTEM table-row frame in one table: All, For review, Analyzed, Archived, Filtered, Queue, Collection, Reference and Draft, each with its own column set, one shown at a time. The Type column's header is a filter that switches the type; All shows every ticket with the All table's columns. Sortable Category / Due date / Status headers, a Status filter on All, and per-row Status dropdowns that recolor the row's status pill.

props.name: types
props.description: [{ id, label, columns, actions, in_all }]. columns: the column keys in order (template.html's COLUMNS: drag (a Reorder handle: drag the row up/down, via table-row), check, save, name, category, due, summary, type, status, status_sort, reason, details, dates, link, notes, updates, actions). actions: the table-cell spec of that type's Actions cell. in_all: whether that type's records appear in the first type's table. The first type is the combined one (All); its label is the Type filter's first item.

props.name: records
props.description: [{ type, status, name, category, due, summary, reason, details, dates, notes, updates }] -- one row each, in its own type's table (and in the first table if its type has in_all). A field a column does not use is ignored; a column whose field is missing renders empty.

props.name: status_options
props.description: [{ value, label }] offered by every Status dropdown and by All's Status filter. value is what the row's data-status becomes (table-row colors the pill for analysed / submitted / approved / pending / declined).

props.name: active
props.description: The type id shown at load. Default: the first type.

rationale: Figma draws each table type as a separate Header + Table pair stacked down the table-row frame; this component puts them in one table so the column sets can be compared by switching. Column sets, header kinds and cell kinds are Figma's (see source): Category and Due date headers carry the sort arrow, All's Status header the filter glyph (icons/filter.svg, node 38:2934), Queue's Status the arrow; Summary / Reason cells are Figma's Single-active-t+button cell (text clipped, "view" kept whole); Status cells are dropdowns whose value is a pill in the row-status colors. One deliberate deviation: Figma's Full Description column is replaced by Type, whose header is the filter that picks the type, so the switch lives in the table's own vocabulary (a filterable column) rather than a separate control; types without Full Description (Collection, Template, Queue) get Type right after Name. Every cell is a real include of table-cell, table-header-cell or table-row; this component adds only the grid (one per type, so header and body share tracks via display:contents rows), the hidden-row fix display:contents needs, and the host wiring the composed components leave to their page (filter, sort, status). All nine types are rendered at build time and hidden, not built by script, because the composed components wire their behavior once at load. Column tracks are token-based: flexible text columns are minmax(spacing-9 x 4, 1fr), everything else max-content (Figma's fixed widths are the width of their content). Actions sit at 40% until row hover (data-reveal-actions), as Figma draws them. An optional `drag` column (blank header, table-row's drag handle) lets a table offer row reordering. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Each type's grid is role="table" labelled with the type's name; hidden tables are removed from the accessibility tree by the hidden attribute. The Type and Status filters are table-header-cell filter buttons (aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-label naming the column and the current choice); the row Status dropdowns carry aria-label "Status of <name>". Rows are grid items via display:contents, so there is no row role; screen readers read the cells in order. Selection, save and dropdown keyboard behavior are the composed components' own.

name: table-row
description: One row of a queue table: a horizontal composition of table-cell instances (checkbox-cell, text cells, status, date, icon-cell, row actions), with a selected state toggled by clicking the row's own checkbox. table-row defines no cell content itself -- it is a flex container that composes table-cell. The demo shows every row Type of the Penpot source with its real cell composition and order, plus a block of rows stacked together with a header row.

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether the row is selected (Penpot's State axis, Default / Selected): its cells fill bg.surface-pressed and its checkbox shows the checked icon, both by CSS off this attribute. Toggled only by clicking the row's own checkbox (component.js).

props.name: status
props.description: Optional data-status on the row (analysed / submitted / approved / pending / declined): style.css colors the value of the row's dropdown-type cell as a status pill from the row-status tokens. Other values, or none, leave it plain.

rationale:
Only Penpot's State axis (Default | Selected) is a style variant. Its other axes -- Type (Checkbox only, Analysed, Found, Archived, Submitted, Empty State, Collection, Check + Button, Snippet) and Comment -- only change which table-cells are composed, never the row's own CSS, so they are demo compositions, not props (as header-block treats its Type axis). Each Type's composition was read off its Penpot instance by x-position, not DOM order: Penpot authors rows in row-reverse with actions first, and this component uses plain left-to-right order, which renders the same and keeps the source readable. Penpot's "Analysed2" appears to be a leftover duplicate and is not demoed; the second, unlabeled checkbox of "Check + Button" is reproduced as it is, with no invented purpose.

Layout (Figma flat table): the row is a flex container with align-items: stretch, so every cell is as tall as the tallest, like a real table row. Hover, focus-within and selected fills go on the cells, not the row, because hosts often lay rows out as display:contents inside a grid (so columns align across rows), and a display:contents element paints nothing. Selected is bg.surface-pressed; data-selected-fill="strong" on the table container uses the darker base/250 (Figma screen 25). Checkbox and save icons show only on hover, focus, selected or saved (the header row always shows them), and data-reveal-actions on the container dims row actions to 40% until hover or keyboard focus, so a long table reads as data first. A row's data-status colors its Status dropdown's value as a pill in the row-status tokens.

Selection: only a click on the row's own checkbox (a checkbox-cell containing [data-icon="checkbox"], so a drag handle in the same cell type is excluded) toggles data-selected; the checked icon swaps in by CSS. Shift+click selects the range from the last clicked row in the same table (visible rows in DOM order, so it follows sorting and skips rows hidden by a search), as one ds-table-row-select event with detail.range = true. A [data-checkbox-group] container may hold one select-all header cell (table-cell checkbox_role="select-all"), whose checked / semi / unchecked state follows how many rows are selected; clicking it selects all unless all are selected.

Reordering: a checkbox-cell holding Penpot's "Drag" glyph is a reorder handle. The row's own script uses native drag and drop, started only from the handle (draggable sits on the handle, which has a box even when the row is display:contents); dragover moves the row before or after the sibling under the pointer, measured on the sibling's first cell, and the dragged row's cells dim to 0.5 -- motion only as feedback. Hosts can drive their own drag and drop instead: data-dragging="true" dims a row, data-drop="before"/"after" draws an accent line on its top or bottom edge, and the whole handle cell shows the grab cursor. Not sourced from the design: selection, range selection, select-all and reordering. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Selection listens only on the row's checkbox cell, so clicks on other cells and their controls never collide with it. No row roles are added (role="row", aria-selected), since the system doesn't wrap rows in a role="table" structure; a host adds them at table level. Known gaps: the row checkbox and the select-all control are role="img" icons with aria-labels ("Select row", "Select all rows"), not real checkboxes, so their checked / mixed state isn't announced, and Shift+click range selection has no keyboard equivalent. The drag handle has aria-label="Reorder", but native drag and drop is pointer-only; an accessible reorder needs a keyboard path (e.g. arrow keys on the focused handle with a live announcement), not implemented. The second checkbox of "Check + Button" is labeled plainly "Checkbox".

name: tag
description: A short label on a colored ground, for categories (accent-1/2/3), statuses (success, warning, danger) or a plain mark (neutral). Active is the solid, high-emphasis form; Passive the light tint for use in quantity, e.g. several tags in one row.

props.name: type
props.description: accent-1 | accent-2 | accent-3 | success | warning | danger | neutral. Sets data-type: which palette color the tag uses.

props.name: subtype
props.description: active (solid fill, white text) or passive (light tint fill, the type's strong color as text). Sets data-subtype. Figma calls these Acive / Passive.

props.name: label
props.description: The tag's text.

rationale: Built from the Figma D_SYSTEM Tag set (node 103:4746): 4px padding (spacing-2), 1px radius (radius-md), body text. Color carries the meaning and nothing else does: each type maps to one palette family (accent primary/secondary/tertiary, signal success/warning/error, neutral). Active uses the strong color as fill; Passive uses the light tint with the strong color as text, so a passive tag keeps its hue at lower weight and several tags in a row stay readable without every one shouting. The colored types use the raw palette on purpose: a category or status color must mean the same in both themes. Neutral is the one theme-aware type (text.active / text.inverced / bg.surface-pressed / text.subactive), because black on the dark surface would disappear. Figma names the warning family 'caution'; this system calls it signal.warning. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Plain inline text in a span, no role: the label itself is the content and is read as text. Color is never the only carrier of meaning -- the label says what the tag is. Passive tags on the light tints keep the strong color as text; the lightest pairs (warning passive) are the lowest contrast in the set, so use warning passive for supplementary marks, not for the only statement of a warning.

name: text-button
description: An unfilled, text-only action control whose color shows the status of the operation behind it (active / loading / confirmed / disabled / error) rather than pointer emphasis -- used where a label must show an async action moving from in-progress to done (e.g. an inline row action). A permanent solid or dotted underline marks it as clickable and says whether the click leaves the page; hover and keyboard focus add '[ ]' brackets.

props.name: priority
props.description: primary (bold typography.buttonPrimary) or secondary (regular typography.buttonSecondary).

props.name: status
props.description: active, loading, disabled, confirmed, or error. status=active, error and disabled carry the permanent underline (see `underline` prop; disabled draws it in the disabled color, Figma D_SYSTEM node 132:4987) -- loading/confirmed are not pointer-interactive states and carry none. error is a destructive-action confirmation state, not a disabled one.

props.name: underline
props.description: solid or dotted -- the permanent underline drawn under the label for status=active, error and disabled: solid when the action navigates to a new page/URL, dotted when it stays within the current view (opens/closes a popup, loads more rows, expands a section). Chosen per instance by what the action does, not by eye (CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions).

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon name (an icons/<name>.svg file), rendered in a `.ds-text-button__icon` span next to a `.ds-text-button__label` span, spacing-button-gap (5px) apart. The icon has no color of its own: it inherits the status color. Omit for a plain text button.

props.name: unread
props.description: data-unread="true": something new behind the button; secondary accent color.

props.name: icon_position
props.description: left or right: where `icon` sits relative to the label (Figma D_SYSTEM Button Type=Text+L-icon / Text+R-icon). right renders the label span first and sets data-icon-position="right". Ignored without `icon`.

props.name: icon_only
props.description: Render only `icon`, no visible label (Figma Type=Icon / icon-outlined). `label` becomes the button's aria-label and title and is required -- template.html fails the compose if it or `icon` is missing. data-icon-only="true"; 10px sides, 8px top/bottom (24px icon in Figma's 44x40 box).

props.name: outlined
props.description: 1px object-dark-passive border around the button (Figma Type=text-outlined / icon-outlined), taken out of the padding so an outlined button's outer box matches the plain one. data-outlined="true".

props.name: preview
props.description: hover: render the hover look (brackets, outlined accent border) without a pointer, via data-preview="hover". Documentation only -- for pages that lay every state side by side (Figma D_SYSTEM node 132:4987); never set it in product UI.

rationale:
Two independent axes, each carried by exactly one property so neither can be misread as the other. Priority changes only typography (typography.buttonPrimary bold vs buttonSecondary regular). Status changes only color, reusing the design's own status vocabulary: active = accent-1 (the one interactive color), loading = system.warning, confirmed = system.success, disabled = object-dark.active, error = system.error-strong where a theme defines it, falling back to system.error. error is a destructive-action confirmation step (e.g. gallery's 'Reset selection' arms a second click): the button is still clickable, the color says what the next click does. The Penpot source's tertiary priority was dropped: it was only partly defined.

Underline: permanent, not hover-only, because the design draws it at rest. It means 'clickable', so it is drawn for active and error; disabled keeps it in the disabled color so the control still says what it would do while the color says it can't; loading and confirmed are not clickable and carry none. solid vs dotted follows the system-wide convention (solid leaves the page, dotted stays in the view; see CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). Solid is 1px (border-width-thin) so it doesn't turn into a bar under bold labels; dotted is 2px (border-width-default) because dot size follows thickness and 1px dots read as specks. The underline sits on an inner span (.ds-text-button__text, added by component.js for bare-text buttons, or .ds-text-button__label) because a browser paints an ancestor's text-decoration across its whole content box, which would include the bracket space.

Brackets: hover and keyboard focus reveal '[ ]' around the label -- the affordance the Penpot source drew on every instance, kept as an interaction cue only. They are always rendered but transparent at rest, so revealing them changes color only and the button never changes width. In tight contexts (header-block rows, sidebar set rows, action/link table cells, page-head, pane and popup-step heads, block-row actions, icon-only buttons) the brackets hang inside the horizontal padding instead of reserving space, so the button hugs its label and neighbours never shift. Outlined buttons show no brackets: their border turns accent-1 on hover and focus instead, the border already being the control's edge.

Box: no fill, no shadow, radius none -- the control is text and color already carries every state. Padding is spacing-cell (10px) vertical / spacing-button-x (11px) horizontal and the icon/bracket gap spacing-button-gap (5px), the figures Figma uses on every button, nav link and table action. Outlined adds the object-dark-passive hairline tables and cards already use, taken out of the padding so an outlined button's outer box matches a plain one. Icon-only buttons pad 8px top/bottom (spacing-3) and 10px sides (spacing-cell) around a 24px (spacing-7) glyph, the size used for standalone glyphs elsewhere.

Icons have no color of their own and inherit the status color, so they track every status without per-status rules; glyphs are inlined via fetch (see component.js) so currentColor applies. unread (accent-2, the nav dot's color) marks that something new is behind the button. preview='hover' draws the hover look statically, for documentation pages only. In dark, system.warning is yellow.600, so loading stays distinct from active. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: Renders as a native <button>. status=disabled also sets the native disabled attribute, since the action is genuinely unavailable. status=loading stays focusable; a host that wants it inert while loading must also set disabled. The permanent underline is supplementary (color already distinguishes the statuses), so forced-colors modes that strip text-decoration remove no information. Icon variants keep .ds-text-button__icon aria-hidden="true": the label already supplies the full accessible name. The hover / focus brackets are CSS-generated ::before/::after content; browsers differ on whether generated content enters the accessible name, so the name never depends on it -- the button's own text is unchanged by hover or focus. Brackets also appear on :focus-visible, so keyboard users get the same affordance as a mouse hover.

name: toast
description: A short confirmation or error message, stacked top center (20px from the top edge), auto-dismissing. May carry one or two action buttons (e.g. links to something just generated). Created at runtime via window.dsToast.show(...), not pre-rendered markup -- see component.js.

props.name: message
props.description: The toast's text.

props.name: status
props.description: "default", "success", "warning" or "error". Picks the color family (Figma D_SYSTEM Toster, node 103:4772): its medium color fills the toast, its strong color draws the border and the close square. success and warning are Figma's; error uses signal.error, default the neutral base grays.

props.name: actions
props.description: Optional array of {label, onClick} (onClick is only meaningful through the real window.dsToast.show() call, not this illustrative template -- see component.js). Up to two.

props.name: duration
props.description: Auto-dismiss delay in ms, only meaningful through window.dsToast.show(). The default (5000) is a judgment call, not a design-source value. 0 (explicit request 2026-10-01) never auto-dismisses: the toast stays until its close button is clicked.

rationale:
Styled to Figma D_SYSTEM's Toster (node 103:4772): a full status fill with a 1px border in the family's strong color, 20px system-message text, and a close button (a 24px square in the strong color with a white X). The fill carries the status at a glance; the X lets a reader drop a toast early instead of waiting out the timer. Figma draws success and warning; default and error follow the same pattern in the neutral and danger families. No shadow: the toast is edged by its border. Status colors are the fixed palette, as everywhere a color states a status, so the text is fixed black in both themes.

Behavior follows the product rule the component was built for: every action that changes stored data produces a short confirmation toast, every failed action an error toast naming the operation and the reason, toasts stack top center, 20px from the top edge (Figma app artboard 345:10101), and auto-dismiss, and a toast may carry actions. Unlike every other component.js, which wires behavior onto markup a page already rendered, a toast only exists because an action just happened, so it exposes a runtime API (window.dsToast.show(...)). Hover and keyboard focus pause the dismiss timer (it restarts at the full duration afterwards, not the remaining time), so a toast with actions doesn't vanish under a reaching cursor or a focused button. The 5000ms default duration is a judgment call; the rule states that toasts auto-dismiss, not how fast. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: role="status" (not role="alert") on each toast: a polite announcement, because toasts report routine results rather than interrupting -- anything that must interrupt uses popup. Action buttons are real, focusable <button> elements from text-button's template. Auto-dismiss is mitigated for mouse (hover pause) and keyboard (focusin/focusout on the toast keeps it alive while an action inside it is focused). Remaining gap: a toast without actions offers nothing to focus, so a screen-reader user reading it gets no pause. The close button is a real <button> with aria-label="Dismiss" (the X is a CSS mask, no text).

name: tooltip
description: A hover/focus tooltip: add data-tooltip="..." directly onto any real element to give it one, no wrapper markup required. E.g. explaining why a disabled Undo button is disabled.

props.name: text
props.description: The tooltip's text. In real usage this is the data-tooltip attribute value on the actual trigger element (a button, an icon span, etc.) -- not a separate component instance.

props.name: label
props.description: Only used by this component's own demo trigger (template.html): the visible content of the illustrative element data-tooltip is attached to. In real use, data-tooltip goes on an element the page already has; this prop has no meaning there.

props.name: preview
props.description: visible: data-preview="visible" on the [data-tooltip] element shows the tooltip without hover/focus. Documentation only (the site's Toasters and tooltips card); never in product UI.

rationale: Styled to Figma D_SYSTEM's Tooltip (node 103:4777): a dark fill (tooltip-bg, Figma base/900), a 1px tooltip-border, white body text, 10px padding, no shadow -- dark so it reads as a layer above the page in either theme. Pure CSS, no JavaScript: content: attr(data-tooltip) reads the trigger's own attribute, and :hover / :focus-visible are the whole show condition, because a tooltip's dismissal is exactly 'stop hovering or focusing'. Adding JS (as popup and dropdown-menu need for their open state) would be complexity with no functional gain. Figma's text+icon variant is not implemented: the bubble is the host's ::after, and a host's ::before is already taken (text-button's hover brackets), so there is no free box for an icon. Known limitation: no viewport clamping, so a trigger near a container edge can render the bubble partly off-screen. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Update 2026-09-30 (explicit request): the bubble is at most a third of the viewport wide and wraps, and a small component.js keeps it on screen -- shifted inside the viewport edges, flipped below when it only fits there, and its text cut at the last word that fits, with an ellipsis, when it fits on neither side. Show/hide stays pure CSS; the script only measures and sets --_tooltip-shift, data-tooltip-placement and data-tooltip-clamped on the trigger.
a11y_notes: :focus-visible (not just :hover) shows the tooltip, so keyboard users reach it with Tab; so does keyboard focus on a control inside the trigger (:has(:focus-visible), 2026-10-03), for a tooltip set on a container such as a table cell around a button. The tooltip text is CSS generated content and is not announced as a description; if it must be announced, the host should add aria-describedby pointing at a real, visually hidden text node. A native <button disabled> can't receive focus, so a tooltip on a disabled button is mouse-only; to make it keyboard-reachable, the host would use aria-disabled on a still-focusable button instead of the disabled attribute.
